title: Launch Brief (DRAFT) — Quickstart Templates (RAG + Agents) v1
body:
Doc status: DRAFT (working launch brief). Owner: Talia Benson (Program Mgmt). Please leave comments inline and tag owners in the “Open questions / decisions” section.

---

1) Executive summary

We are launching Redwood Inference “Quickstart Templates” for production-minded RAG + agent applications. The goal is to get a developer from sign-up → first successful request → deployable, observable app with safe defaults.

This launch includes:
- Template repos (Python + TypeScript) with a consistent structure, safe networking defaults, and clear operational hooks (metrics/traces/logs).
- A small scaffolding CLI (init + doctor) to reduce setup friction and validate local environment.
- Prebuilt observability pack dashboards + recommended alerting rules.
- Docs-site integration (new Quickstart Templates section, walkthrough, troubleshooting, observability reference).

High-level outcome we want: fewer “blank slate” projects, faster activation, fewer onboarding tickets, and better-quality signals for SRE/support when users do hit issues.

---

2) Audience + target personas

Primary audience (PLG):
- Full-stack / backend engineers building an LLM feature (doc search, support copilots, internal knowledge assistants).
- ML engineers prototyping RAG pipelines who need a clean path to production hygiene.

Secondary audience (sales-assisted / platform teams):
- Platform and infrastructure teams standardizing inference and observability across squads.
- Security-conscious teams evaluating Dedicated or Private deployments who need clear guidance on secrets and redaction.

Non-target (for v1):
- Teams seeking a “no-code” builder.
- Teams requiring a full, opinionated UI + multi-tenant auth stack out of the box.
- Complex multi-agent orchestration frameworks (v1 includes a minimal agent loop with tool calling + guardrails; not a comprehensive agent platform).

---

3) What we’re launching (scope)

3.1 Templates (v1)

A) RAG + Agents — Python
- Minimal API server (streaming-capable)
- Retrieval pipeline with a retriever interface and pluggable vector store adapters (local default + optional hosted placeholder)
- Agent loop with tool calling
- Guardrails: max iterations, tool output size limits, tool schema validation patterns
- Eval hooks: golden prompts + run_eval script for regression
- Safe defaults: timeouts, retries/backoff, token/cost caps, sane concurrency defaults

B) RAG + Agents — TypeScript
- Parity structure with Python where possible
- Streaming robustness patterns and better error typing
- Structured output parsing + tool schema validation patterns
- OTel-friendly hooks/middleware points for instrumentation

3.2 Template CLI
- `init`: scaffold chosen template + write a version stamp
- `doctor`: validate env vars (API key, model config), API connectivity, collector health; print actionable remediation

Notes:
- Upgrade story is “lightweight” in v1: we will document how to re-init into a new directory / compare changes, not guarantee in-place upgrades for customized apps.

3.3 Observability pack integration
- OpenTelemetry traces + metrics emitted by template apps
- Prebuilt dashboards:
  - RAG latency breakdown (retrieval vs generation)
  - Tool failure rate and tool latency
  - Retrieval hit rate / empty results
  - Token economics and error rate
- Recommended alert rules + SLO examples (with guidance to avoid noisy defaults)

3.4 Docs-site integration
- New “Quickstart Templates” section and navigation updates
- Walkthrough: setup, run, deploy notes
- Troubleshooting page (top issues: 401/403, 429, timeouts, tool schema failures, empty retrieval)
- Observability hooks reference (span names, attributes, metric names, redaction)

---

4) Positioning + messaging

One-liner:
“Quickstart Templates help you ship a production-minded RAG or agent app on Redwood in minutes—safe defaults, observable by default, and easy to deploy.”

Key messages (what to emphasize):
1) Production-minded by default
- Safe networking defaults (timeouts/retries), streaming resilience, and cost controls
- Opinionated but not locked-in: provider abstraction and config-driven model pinning

2) Observable out of the box
- Standard traces/metrics/logs (OpenTelemetry + Redwood conventions)
- Prebuilt dashboards + recommended alerts so teams can operate day-2

3) Faster time-to-first-success
- CLI reduces “paper cuts” (env validation, collector checks)
- Docs and troubleshooting reflect real failure modes we see in support

4) Designed to be a starting point, not magic
- Templates are scaffolds: you still own your app’s auth, data, and production policies

Claims we should avoid (or qualify):
- “Production-ready for every enterprise out of the box” (instead: “production-minded scaffolding with safe defaults and observability conventions”)
- “No vendor lock-in” (instead: “minimal lock-in and a provider abstraction; Redwood instrumentation can be disabled or swapped”) 

---

5) Changelog highlights (v1)

Template developer experience
- Standardized README format across templates (setup → run → verify observability → troubleshooting)
- Clear env var schema + validation utilities (shared patterns)
- Dockerfile + docker-compose including local OTel collector

Resilience + safe defaults
- Timeouts and retries/backoff aligned across templates
- Streaming stability patterns + smoke tests to catch regressions
- Circuit breaker-style behaviors for repeated failures (where applicable)

Agents + RAG baseline
- Tool calling agent loop with guardrails
- Retriever abstraction + vector store adapters
- Structured output and tool schema validation patterns

Observability
- Consistent span hierarchy and naming
- Required attributes and redaction rules
- Dashboards + alert examples published in observability pack

Telemetry for adoption metrics (IMPORTANT: privacy + compatibility)
- Optional tagging to identify template-originated traffic for KPI measurement
- Must be opt-in and avoid PII; no prompt/content logging
- Known risk: some corporate proxies reject unknown headers; we provide a “disable telemetry tags” default and document how to enable

---

6) Rollout plan

6.1 Phases

Phase 0 — Internal beta (done / ongoing hardening)
- Audience: Redwood internal engineers + Solutions Engineering + Support
- Goals: catch setup friction, verify dashboards, validate troubleshooting accuracy
- Inputs: Slack #help threads + early support tickets + internal dogfooding notes

Phase 1 — External beta (timeboxed)
- Audience: a small set of friendly customers and inbound self-serve users
- Entry criteria:
  - Python + TS templates pass CI smoke tests (streaming + tools)
  - Docs walkthrough + troubleshooting published
  - Observability dashboards validated end-to-end (collector → backend → Console)
  - Telemetry tagging is opt-in and documented
- Exit criteria:
  - ≥80% of beta users reach “first success” without DevEx intervention (see metrics definition)
  - Top 10 issues have a documented workaround or are fixed

Phase 2 — Public launch (GA)
- Docs nav + templates promoted as primary onboarding path for RAG/agents
- Template repos versioned and releases cut
- Support playbooks and escalation paths finalized

6.2 Tentative timeline (subject to change)
- Week 1: finalize docs + troubleshooting + instrumentation reference; validate dashboards (Allison/Sergio)
- Week 2: external beta start; monitor support + funnel; ship 1–2 patch releases
- Week 4: public launch decision meeting + comms + enablement

(We will replace with specific dates once we align owners’ availability and support coverage.)

6.3 Launch channels
- Docs homepage / navigation inclusion
- Redwood Console “Getting Started” link to templates
- Minimal blog post or changelog entry (optional for v1; decision pending)
- Social/community post (developer advocate optional)

---

7) Success metrics + measurement plan

Primary KPIs
1) Time-to-first-success (TTFS)
- Definition (proposed): time from first template download/init to first successful streaming response from the app using Redwood API.
- We will track via:
  - CLI events (init/doctor success) where possible
  - Template traffic tagging (opt-in) for “template-originated” requests
  - Docs funnel events (template page views → repo/CLI actions)

2) Activation rate
- % of users who start with templates and make ≥N successful requests within 24h

3) Support deflection
- Reduction in onboarding tickets for RAG/agents compared to baseline (e.g., 401/429/timeouts/tool parse errors)
- Quality improvement in tickets that do occur (request IDs present, clearer error taxonomy)

4) Retention (template usage)
- % of template starters still making traffic after 7/30 days (proxy via tagged traffic, where enabled)

Secondary
- Observability coverage rate: % of runs with valid trace IDs + required span attributes
- Error taxonomy completeness: % of failures categorized into standard buckets

Owners
- KPI definitions + dashboard: Nikhil Sharma (PM) + Logan Wright (telemetry liaison)
- Instrumentation standards: Allison Grant
- Docs funnel events: Elliot Price + Wei Chen

Privacy / data handling constraints
- No prompts or retrieved content logged by default
- Telemetry tagging must not encode user identifiers or content
- Provide clear documentation: “what we collect” + how to disable

---

8) Internal enablement checklist

8.1 Support readiness (Dev Patel / Priya Shah)
- [ ] Support playbook drafted: common issues, triage steps, known workarounds
- [ ] Troubleshooting page matches top support issues (401/403, 429, timeouts, collector misconfig, proxy header issues)
- [ ] Escalation policy: when to route to DevEx vs SDK teams vs Observability/SRE
- [ ] Ensure request ID propagation guidance is in place (collect request ID, trace ID, template version stamp)

8.2 SRE / Observability readiness (Christine Wong / Allison Grant / Sergio Costa)
- [ ] Dashboards published + verified with a fresh template app
- [ ] Alert examples reviewed for noise/cardinality risks
- [ ] Redaction defaults validated (no secrets/PII in spans/logs)
- [ ] “How to verify telemetry” script and instructions included in docs

8.3 Docs readiness (Elliot Price / Wei Chen)
- [ ] Docs IA updated and approved
- [ ] Walkthrough includes: setup, run, verify observability, deploy options, cost controls
- [ ] Troubleshooting page includes copy-pastable commands and symptoms → fixes mapping
- [ ] Notes on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private considerations included where relevant (networking, collector endpoints, auth)

8.4 SDK / API readiness (Monica Patel / Ibrahim Khan / Dana Lo)
- [ ] SDK defaults match template safe defaults (timeouts/retries) or templates clearly override
- [ ] Streaming reconnect/error types stable enough for template usage
- [ ] Request ID extraction + propagation helpers available

8.5 Security review (Marcus Lin / Kaitlyn Nguyen / Hanae Suzuki)
- [ ] Dependency pinning + vulnerability scanning enabled in template repos
- [ ] Secrets handling guidance in README (dotenv usage, never commit keys)
- [ ] Sample data policy compliant; no real customer data
- [ ] Logging redaction verified (headers, keys, sensitive env vars)

8.6 Release/versioning readiness (Connor O’Brien)
- [ ] Versioning policy documented (latest vs pinned)
- [ ] Changelog + deprecation policy draft
- [ ] Release cut checklist in repo (tagging, docs link updates)

---

9) Post-launch feedback loop + operating cadence

Cadence
- Week 0–2 after launch: daily triage of issues + quick patches
- Week 3–6: weekly triage + biweekly release train

Inputs
- Support tickets tagged “quickstart-templates”
- GitHub issues/PRs in redwood-quickstarts
- Docs feedback widget + broken-link reports
- Console metrics (activation funnel, tagged traffic where enabled)

Triage meeting
- Owner: Talia Benson
- Attendees: Monica Patel, Elliot Price, Allison Grant, Dev Patel (as needed)
- Agenda:
  1) Top activation blockers
  2) Top support drivers
  3) Observability gaps
  4) Security/regression concerns
  5) Release decision (patch vs minor)

Definition of “launch blocker”
- Cannot complete setup/run steps following docs on a clean machine
- Streaming disconnect loops with no mitigation guidance
- Tool schema validation failures with confusing errors/no workaround
- Collector config failures without actionable error messages
- Any evidence of secrets/PII being logged by default

---

10) Known risks + mitigations

Risk: Corporate proxies reject unknown headers (template telemetry tagging)
- Mitigation: telemetry tags opt-in; default off; document environment flag to enable/disable; avoid hard dependency on headers

Risk: High-cardinality attributes in traces/metrics
- Mitigation: follow Observability conventions; limit dimensions/tags; review any new attributes with Allison/Caleb

Risk: CI flakiness in streaming smoke tests
- Mitigation: isolate tests, add retry with bounds, increase timeouts cautiously, use deterministic fixtures, track flake rate

Risk: Users interpret “agent template” as a Redwood product feature
- Mitigation: careful terminology in README/docs (agent loop example, not a managed agent product); include “What this is / isn’t” section

Risk: Dependency drift and security vulnerabilities in templates
- Mitigation: pinned deps + scanning workflow + documented upgrade process; defined owners for monthly dependency bumps

---

11) Open questions / decisions (need owners + due dates)

1) Telemetry defaults
- Decision needed: default OFF for template-origin tags (recommended) vs ON with fallback
- Owner: Nikhil Sharma + Marcus Lin

2) Which deployment recipes to highlight in v1 docs (Docker/Fly/Render/k8s)
- Decision needed: choose 1–2 “happy path” options to keep scope tight
- Owner: Elliot Price + Monica Patel

3) Supported model list + pinning guidance
- Decision needed: which Redwood-verified models are default; what fallback policy we recommend
- Owner: Henry Cho

4) External beta cohort
- Decision needed: list of 5–10 accounts + criteria + comms owner
- Owner: Renee Sullivan + Solutions Engineering (TBD)

5) GA gate
- Decision needed: threshold for TTFS + activation + support ticket volume to proceed
- Owner: Alex Martinez + Talia Benson

---

12) Appendix: Draft announcement copy (internal)

Subject: Quickstart Templates (RAG + Agents) — internal beta

Body (draft):
“We’ve published the first version of Redwood Quickstart Templates for RAG + Agents (Python + TypeScript). They’re opinionated scaffolds with safe defaults, built-in OpenTelemetry instrumentation, and a small CLI (init + doctor) to reduce setup friction. Please try them end-to-end, verify the dashboards, and file issues for anything that blocks a clean setup. When reporting issues, include your template version stamp, Redwood request IDs, and any trace IDs.”

---

Notes to self / backlog items (not part of v1 launch criteria)
- Add a UI-oriented RAG template (frontend + auth) once core infra is stable
- Add more vector store adapters (keep optional to avoid lock-in)
- Add “upgrade” command for CLI if we can define a safe story
- Add more eval scenarios (hallucination checks, retrieval adversarial prompts) once harness is stable
